issues.desc: background.md Key Insights and Solution Tradeoffs use jargon terms "3x2 escalation" and "3x1 fallback" without expanding them on first appearance. A new reader cannot tell whether 3x2 means 3-reviewer×2-pass quorum or something else. These should be defined inline or in a short parenthetical.

background.md Key Insights states .Codex/ has 18 files inside it ("18 files inside .Codex/ itself need git mv"), but find counts 20 actual tracked files in .Codex/. The undercount may lead the implementer to miss 2 files. (Verified: find .Codex -type f | wc -l = 20.)

background.md Key Insights states "32 tracked files reference .Codex/" outside the directory, but git grep -l counts approximately 48–49 files referencing .Codex outside .lattice/.Codex/.codex. CHK-002 context lists only ~20 specific filenames to update. The ~16-file gap is material scope risk. The checklist grep-based verification command (git grep -nE) will catch residuals at done-time, but the mismatch is a factual inaccuracy in the background. (Verified: git grep -l .Codex -- . :(exclude).lattice :(exclude).Codex :(exclude).codex | wc -l = 48.)

background.md states omx removal touches "23 files" ("13 + 10 decision docs"), but git grep -l -i omx (excluding .lattice and CHANGELOG) counts 35 distinct files. The 12-file scope gap may cause incomplete removal. CHK-003 has a post-condition grep to catch residuals, which mitigates the risk, but the stated count is factually inaccurate.

background.md Solution Tradeoffs refers to "(memory)" as a shorthand for the user-approved degraded 3x1 fallback policy, but "memory" as a system concept (Claude memory store / MEMORY.md) is not defined inline. A reader without access to the memory file cannot verify this approval was actually granted. Consider citing the specific memory key (e.g., \"use-degraded-3x1-review-escalation.md\") directly in the background.
